predecessors.name: Kenmu Restoration
predecessors.text: the realm of Go-Daigo's restored imperial government, which Takauji overthrew ('Ashikaga Takauji was appointed Shōgun after overthrowing the Kenmu Restoration')

successors.name: Warring States Japan
successors.text: the shogunate's last holding around Kyoto, which Oda Nobunaga took when he 'drove Yoshiaki out of Kyoto' in 1573

ledger.x: 1336: the war for Kyushu begins. the page has Takauji allying with local Kyushu clans after retreating there in 1336, and imperial resistance in Kyushu lasting until the end of the period; it does not date the first Southern Court campaign in Kyushu, so 1336 is the retreat.
1336: Ashikaga Takauji sets up his military government in Kyoto.
1336: the shogunate takes over the Kenmu court's realm on paper.
1337: Go-Daigo sets up the Southern Court at Yoshino.
1392: the Southern Court yields and the two courts are one.
1459: the Twelve Garrisons of Dōnan on the southern Oshima Peninsula are held by the Wajin again.
1467: the Ōnin War breaks out in Kyoto.
1468: outside Kyoto the shogunate no longer rules.
1477: the Ōnin War ends. Ōuchi Masahiro 'left the area on 17 December 1477'; 'By 1477, ten years after the fighting had begun, Kyoto was nothing more than a place for mobs to loot.'
1573: Oda Nobunaga drives Ashikaga Yoshiaki out of Kyoto and the shogunate ends.

wars.name: Nanboku-chō wars (Northern and Southern Courts)
wars.outcome: Ashikaga victory: Kyushu resistance collapsed in 1381 and the last domain submitted in 1385; on 19 November 1392 Go-Kameyama yielded the Imperial Regalia to the Northern Court.

wars.name: Kannō disturbance
wars.outcome: Tadayoshi rebelled in 1350 and joined the Southern Court; he beat Takauji in 1351 and died suddenly in March 1352 after a second reconciliation.

wars.name: Koshamain's revolt
wars.outcome: Wajin victory: the Ainu took 10 of the 12 garrisons in May 1457; Takeda Nobuhiro's counteroffensive in 1458 killed Koshamain and his son at Nanaehama.

wars.name: Ōnin War
wars.outcome: Ten years of fighting in Kyoto and Yamashiro that left the shogunate 'reduced to little more than a local political force in Kyoto' and began the Sengoku period; the Western Army's last major lord, Ōuchi Masahiro, left on 17 December 1477.

wars.name: Oda Nobunaga's entry into Kyoto and expulsion of Yoshiaki
wars.outcome: Nobunaga marched on Kyoto in 1568 'to support the 15th shogun, Ashikaga Yoshiaki' and 'expelled Ashikaga Yoshiaki from Kyoto in 1573, thus destroying the Ashikaga shogunate'.

certainty.note: Feudal shugo and daimyo domains with no surveyed frontiers: the national outline to 1467 is the claimed realm, the Kyushu and Yoshino fronts with the Southern Court are approximate, and the post-1468 Kyoto remnant is drawn from…
